name: On/Off Module

productKeyVerification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) marks the product Legacy, made before product keys, so it doesn't answer Product Data Request. Later firmware versions run i2CS, as this profile's engine entries give, and may answer with a key; none is documented for them.

verification.note: Read from the product having one load, which its group 1 controls, as on other one-load products.

steps.text: Plug the lamp or device (the load) you want to control into the outlet on the bottom of the module, with the load's own switch in the on position.
Plug the module into an unswitched wall outlet.
steps.expect: Status LED and the load turn on

steps.text: If the load does not turn on, turn it on with the switch on the load itself.
Tap the SET button to toggle the load on and off.

notes: Do not plug the module into a switched outlet, a filtered power strip or an AC line filter, and do not stack Insteon modules.
The pass-through outlet on the front works as an ordinary uncontrolled outlet; do not plug another home automation product into it.
After installation the load's own switch no longer controls it unless load sensing is enabled.

steps.text: Use the SET button to set the module to the state you want the controller to activate (on or off).
With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the module's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes twice and then turns on solid

notes: The module links as a responder: set the controller to linking mode first (for most controllers, press and hold an On or scene button for 10 seconds or the SET button for 3 seconds), then press and hold this module's SET button.

Pressing and holding the SET button for 3 seconds on its own puts the module in linking mode (Status LED blinks) for four minutes; the On/Off Module 2456S3 Owner's Manual uses this to assign an X10 address.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the module's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes twice and then turns on solid

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) says i1 devices don't support Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), and the catalog doesn't know the engine of every version of this product. An i2 or i2CS version takes it; ask the device with Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) first.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: With the controller in unlinking mode, press and hold the module's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes twice and then turns on solid

notes: To unlink, set the controller to unlinking mode first (for most controllers, press and hold an On or scene button for 10 seconds twice or the SET button for 3 seconds twice), then press and hold this module's SET button for 3 seconds.

steps.text: Unlink the module from any controller that controls it.
Unplug the module.
Wait about 10 seconds.
While holding down the SET button, plug the module back in without letting go of the button.
Keep holding the SET button for 3 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes once and turns off; after a few seconds the Status LED and the load turn on

steps.text: Unlink the module from every controller it is linked to.

notes: The On/Off Module 2456S3 Owner's Manual says to unlink the module from all controllers before you stop using it; otherwise the controllers keep retrying commands and slow the system.
If an X10 primary address was assigned, remove it as well so the module does not keep responding to X10 commands.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove the modem's group 0 link with no SET button press: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the On/Off Module 2456S3 Owner's Manual gives it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)
